nodes.summary: A real vector space $E$ with a topology is of type (B) when there is a function $\|\cdot\| : E \to \mathbb{R}$ with $\|x\| \ge 0$, with $\|x\| = 0$ exactly when $x = 0$, with $\|x + y\| \le \|x\| + \|y\|$ and with $\|a x\| = |a| \, \|x\|$ for all $x, y \in E$ and $a \in \mathbb{R}$, such that a set $U \subseteq E$ is open exactly when every $x \in U$ has an $\varepsilon > 0$ with $y \in U$ whenever…
nodes.title: Spaces of type (B)

nodes.summary: The Mazur–Orlicz claim of Problem 15.1 is false: there is a real vector space $E$ with a topology that is of type (F) and contains a bounded sphere, but is not of type (B).
nodes.title: Negative answer to Scottish Book Problem 15.1

nodes.summary: The claim of Scottish Book Problem 26 is false: there are a real vector space $E$ with a topology, of type $\{F_o\}$, and a sequence $(F_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$ that converges to $0$ uniformly on every bounded subset of $E$ but does not converge to $0$ uniformly on any open set containing $0$.
nodes.title: Mazur and Orlicz's Problem 26 has a negative answer

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology. A set $R \subseteq E$ is bounded if for every sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of points of $R$ and every real sequence $(t_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $t_n \to 0$, we have $t_n x_n \to 0$ in $E$.
nodes.title: Bounded sets in Scottish Book Problem 26

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology. A set $R \subseteq E$ is bounded when for every sequence $(x_n)$ of points of $R$ and every sequence $(t_n)$ of real numbers with $t_n \to 0$, the sequence $(t_n x_n)$ tends to $0$ in $E$.
nodes.title: Sequentially bounded sets

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space. A set $K \subseteq E$ is a sphere when $0 \notin K$ and for every $x \ne 0$ in $E$ there is exactly one real $t > 0$ with $t x \in K$; that is, every open ray from the origin meets $K$ exactly once.
nodes.title: Spheres in the ray sense

nodes.summary: A real vector space $E$ with a topology is of type (F) if there is a metric $d$ on $E$ that induces its topology, is translation invariant, $d(x + z, y + z) = d(x, y)$ for all $x, y, z \in E$, and is complete, and if addition $E \times E \to E$ and scalar multiplication $\mathbb{R} \times E \to E$ are continuous.
nodes.title: Spaces of type (F) in Scottish Book Problem 26

nodes.summary: A real vector space $E$ with a topology is of type (F) when addition $E \times E \to E$ and scalar multiplication $\mathbb{R} \times E \to E$ are continuous and there is a metric $d$ on $E$ that is translation invariant, $d(x + z, y + z) = d(x, y)$ for all $x, y, z \in E$, that induces the topology of $E$, and that is complete: every Cauchy sequence for $d$ converges for $d$.
nodes.title: Spaces of type (F)

nodes.summary: A real vector space $E$ with a topology is of type $\{F_o\}$ if it is of type (F) and, for every sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $E$ with $x_n \to 0$ and every real sequence $(t_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $\sum_n |t_n| < \infty$, the series $\sum_n t_n x_n$ converges in $E$.
nodes.title: Spaces of type $\{F_o\}$

nodes.summary: The claim of Mazur and Orlicz that every real vector space $E$ with a topology that is of type (F) and contains a bounded sphere is of type (B).
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 15.1

nodes.summary: The claim that for every real vector space $E$ with a topology that is of type $\{F_o\}$ and every sequence $(F_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$, if $F_n \to 0$ uniformly on every bounded set $R \subseteq E$, then there is an open set $U \subseteq E$ containing $0$ on which $F_n \to 0$ uniformly.
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 26 (Mazur and Orlicz's claim)

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
